alex: Heads-up: I'm handing off primary for the 07:00-15:00 shift to maria. Leaving notes below — we had a few noisy alerts overnight but cleared. ping @maria @jamal for gaps.

maria: ack. quick Q — who is secondary? last rota shows jamal but I see jamal on PTO til 11:00.

alex: jamal is nominal secondary but yes partial coverage 07-11. sasha agreed to fill 07-09 via DM. After 09 we are one person until jamal back. tagging @sasha

sasha: can confirm I'll cover 07-09. I'll monitor pages and take escalation if latency SLO > 350ms for generation endpoints.

jamal: back at 11:05. if anything critical before then escalate to oncall lead (maria) or me after 11.

incident-bot: Incident alert: model-serving-latency-high (P2) — 1789998601

alex: that was from the earlier flapping. summary: regen queues grew due to a bad autoscaler config after deploy. fixed by reverting autoscaler and restarting inference-nodes; check runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency

maria: thanks. can you paste quick remediation steps for the runbook? want a short checklist to pin in case we get the same page.

alex: short checklist:
1) Check dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/r/latency?svc=inference
2) If pod CPU > 85% on all nodes: scale up pool or revert autoscaler:
```
kubectl rollouts undo deployment/inference-autoscaler -n redwood
kubectl get pods -l app=inference -n redwood -o wide
```
3) If mem/kv-cache pressure: restart kv-proxy on affected nodes:
```
kubectl exec -n redwood kv-proxy-<pod> -- supervisorctl restart kv-proxy
```
4) Fallback routing: enable model-variant fallback (console -> routes -> enable fallback) or via CLI:
```
redwoodctl routes set --fallback small-llama --route inference
```
5) Notify oncall-channel and customers via status page if >15min impact.

maria: nice. also add quick commands to clear prefix cache if stale keys:

alex: good call. prefix cache flush:
```
redwoodctl cache flush --type=prefix --prefix "user-" --region us-west1
```
Note: flushing cache may increase token cost briefly.

sasha: I keep a minimal checklist in my phone. Suggest we pin these to the shift handoff doc: https://redwood.internal/ops/shift-handoff

jamal: Anything for model OOMs? saw a tokenization spike once.

alex: yes — OOM quick steps:
- check pod logs for OOMKilled
- reduce max_tokens per request via rate-limiting or policy in api-gateway
- restart the failing model container (kubectl delete pod)
- promote a smaller quantized variant via model-catalog: https://redwood.internal/models/catalog

maria: Good. Any open follow-ups for this shift?

alex: two:
- confirm autoscaler rollforward test scheduled (ie, test in staging): https://cal.redwood.com/event/rollforward-test
- update runbook with the `redwoodctl cache flush` note and OOM checklist (assign to jamal)

jamal: I'll update runbook by EOD and leave a changelog entry.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: revert-autoscaler-rollback (success) — 1789999005

maria: all right I'll be primary. sasha covers 07-09, jamal covers 11- end. If paging during coverage gap escalate to oncall-lead. Pinning the checklist here.

alex: thanks y'all. Adding a snippet to handoff doc with the quick-check list so it's one click for the next person: https://redwood.internal/ops/shift-handoff#quick-checks

sasha: 👍

maria: leaving a quick status update for customers if we hit >15m: draft message:
"We are aware of increased inference latency affecting a subset of requests in us-west1. Our engineers have reverted an autoscaler change and are monitoring. No data loss. We'll update within 30 minutes." 

alex: LGTM

jamal: +1

incident-bot: Incident resolved: model-serving-latency-high — 1789999120

maria: closing handoff: primary=maria, secondary=jamal (partial until 11), ad-hoc cover=sasha 07-09. runbook links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-latency , https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oom-handling , https://redwood.internal/ops/shift-handoff . file updated by jamal.

sasha: noted. I'll leave my monitoring dashboard open.

alex: thanks team, signing off.
